(men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] | years11 = 2026–present | team11 = [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] | highlights = * [[ABA League]] champion ([[2023–24 ABA League First Division|2024]]) * [[German Basketball Cup|German Cup]] winner ([[2022–23 BBL-Pokal|2023]]) * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Most Improved Player ([[2019–20 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|2020]]) * Second-team All-Big 12 (2020) * Big 12 All-Defensive Team (2020) * Second-team All-[[Minnesota Intercollegiate Athletic Conference|MIAC]] (2017) }} '''Frederick Gillespie''' (born June 14, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Carleton Knights men's basketball|Carleton Knights]] and the [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor Bears]]. ==Early life== Gillespie grew up in [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]] and played football growing up until trying basketball in eighth grade.{{cite web|url=https://www.twincities.com/2020/01/17/late-blooming-freddie-gillespie-goes-from-east-ridge-role-player-to-baylor-beast/|title=Late-blooming Freddie Gillespie goes from East Ridge role player to Baylor beast|last=Frederick|first=Jace|work=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]|date=January 17, 2020|access-date=February 3, 2020}} He entered [[East Ridge High School (Minnesota)|East Ridge High School]] at 5'11" and did not play basketball his freshman year, after breaking his ankle on the first day of team tryouts. He grew to 6'4" by the time he was a sophomore, and subsequently played on the junior [[varsity team]]. Gillespie played varsity ball as a junior but [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|tore his ACL]] late in the season, causing him to miss the summer [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] circuit.{{cite web|url=https://www.wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/gillespie-makes-big-leap-major-impact-for-baylor-men/article_608cb96e-d0b1-5487-9bb6-c415c19f6e2a.html|title=Gillespie makes big leap, major impact for Baylor men|first=John|last=Werner|work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]]|date=February 15, 2019|access-date=February 3, 2020}} He finally returned to the court healthy in his senior season, although Gillespie did not receive any all-conference honors. After receiving no Division I or II scholarship offers, Gillespie opted to attend Division III [[Carleton College]].{{cite web|url=http://dailyorange.com/2019/03/no-idea-happen-freddie-gillespies-rise-d-iii-player-important-baylor-big/|title='No idea this would happen': Freddie Gillespie's rise from a D-III player to an important Baylor big|first=Billy|last=Heyen|work=The Daily Orange|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=February 3, 2020}} ==College career== [[File:Freddie Gillespie.jpg|thumb|upright=.6|left|Gillespie playing for Baylor in 2019]]Gillespie started his collegiate career at Division III Carleton College, choosing the school due to its academic pedigree. He played only 16 total minutes in his true freshman season despite being, in his words, “the most athletic, biggest guy in that whole [[Athletic conference|conference]]." As a sophomore, Gillespie averaged 10.0 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.6 blocks per game, shooting 53.2 percent from the field. He was named second-team All-[[Minnesota Intercollegiate Athletic Conference]].{{cite web|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2019/11/08/i-had-no-idea-id-end-up-being-here-freddie-gillespies-path-from-division-iii-to-baylor-starter/|title='I had no idea I'd end up being here': Freddie Gillespie's path from Division III to Baylor starter|first=Travis|last=Hines|website=[[NBCSports.com]]|date=November 8, 2019|access-date=February 3, 2020}} Following the season, he decided to attempt to transfer to a Division I program. A friend of Gillespie's mother, former [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] player and assistant coach Al Nuness, was able to put him in contact with Baylor coach [[Scott Drew]] through his son, Jared Nuness, a member of the Baylor coaching staff.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/late-blooming-big-man-attempts-make-leap-division-iii-baylor-093822817.html|title=Late-blooming big man attempts to make the leap from Division III to Baylor|first=Jeff|last=Eisenberg|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=June 8, 2017|access-date=February 3, 2020}} Gillespie joined the Baylor basketball team as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]], sitting out a year due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] transfer rules and then earning a scholarship.{{cite web|url=https://www.wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/baylor-walk-on-gillespie-gets-men-s-basketball-scholarship/article_f7938bcb-4b1b-5610-ad7b-14e3569bf45d.html|title=Baylor walk-on Gillespie gets men's basketball scholarship|work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]]|date=May 17, 2018|access-date=February 3, 2020}} As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt junior]], he averaged 5.3 points and 4.4 rebounds per game in 26 games played.{{cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/surprise-surprise-freddie-gillespie-s-leap-from-low-level-hoops-to-final-four-dreams/567063212/|title=Surprise, surprise: Freddie Gillespie's leap from low-level hoops to Final Four dreams|first=Marcus|last=Fuller|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=January 17, 2020|access-date=February 3, 2020}} On December 9, 2019, Gillespie was named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Player of the Week after contributing 17 points, 13 rebounds, and five blocks in a win over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].{{cite web|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2019/12/9/first-time-honorees-receive-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|title=First Time Honorees Receive Men's Basketball Awards|publisher=Big 12 Conference|date=December 9, 2019|access-date=February 4, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Gillespie was named Big 12 Most Improved Player, Second Team All-Big 12 and to the All-Defensive Team after averaging 9.6 points, 9.0 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game.{{cite press release|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/7/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx|title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=March 8, 2020 |access-date=March 8, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.twincities.com/2020/03/13/this-year-minnesotans-took-over-college-basketball-hows-our-best-of-the-best/|title=This year, Minnesotans took over college basketball. Here's our best of the best.|work=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]|date=March 13, 2020|access-date=March 24, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Hustle (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Gillespie signed a training camp contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]],{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign eight, including Barea, Iwundu, Burke|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-six-including-barea-iwundu-burke/|work=Mavs.com|date=December 1, 2020|access-date=December 1, 2020}} but didn't make the final roster.{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks briefs: These players are 'dumb and dumber,' plus roster is set|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-briefs-12-19/|website=Mavs.com|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=December 19, 2020}} On January 11, 2021, the [[Memphis Hustle]] selected Gillespie with the 2nd pick overall in the 2020–2021 [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|NBA G League draft]].{{cite web|title=NBA G League 2020–21 Draft Results|url=https://gleague.nba.com/nba-g-league-2020-21-draft-order/|website=NBA.com|date=January 11, 2021|access-date=February 1, 2021}} In 15 games, he averaged 10.5 points, 10.3 rebounds and 2.3 blocks in 27.8 minutes while shooting .570 from the field and recording six double-doubles.{{cite web|first=Soheil|last=Jamshidi|title=Raptors Sign Gillespie To 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-gillespie-10-day-contract|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2021|access-date=April 8, 2021}} ===Toronto Raptors (2021)=== On April 8, 2021, Gillespie signed a 10-day contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]]. Two days later, he made his debut with the Raptors, recording six points, four rebounds, one assist, three steals and one block in 18 minutes during a 135–115 win against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=Trent scores career-high 44, Raptors rout Cavaliers 135–115|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/recap?gameId=401307587|work=ESPN.com|date=April 10, 2021|access-date=April 11, 2021}} On April 14, in a 122–117 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]], he scored 9 points, grabbed 8 rebounds and recorded 2 blocks, all career-highs.{{cite web|title=Anunoby, Siakam rally Raptors past Spurs 117–112|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401307626|work=ESPN.com|date=April 14, 2021|access-date=April 16, 2021}} Two days later, he reached a new career-high of 10 points, with seven rebounds, in a 113–102 win against the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=Watson, Watanabe lead Raptors past Magic, 113-02|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401307645|work=ESPN.com|date=April 16, 2021|access-date=April 18, 2021}} On April 18, Gillespie signed a second 10-day contract{{cite web|first=Soheil|last=Jamshidi|title=Raptors Sign Gillespie To A Second 10-day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-gillespie-second-10-day-contract|work=NBA.com|date=April 18, 2021|access-date=April 18, 2021}} and tied his career-high with 10 points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal, going a perfect 4 of 4 from the field in a 112–106 win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|title=Boucher, Raptors hand Thunder 10th straight loss, 112–106|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401307662|work=ESPN.com|date=April 18, 2021|access-date=April 21, 2021}} Three days later, he had four points, five rebounds, and a career-high five blocks in a 114–103 win against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Raptors ride strong 3rd quarter to 114–103 win over Nets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401307684|work=ESPN.com|date=April 21, 2021|access-date=April 23, 2021}} On April 28, Gillespie signed for the remainder of the season.{{cite web|first=Soheil|last=Jamshidi|title=Raptors Sign Gillespie|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-gillespie|work=NBA.com|date=April 28, 2021|access-date=April 28, 2021}} He was represented by sports agency Beyond Athlete Management. On May 2, 2021, Gillespie had a new career-high of 11 points, with seven rebounds and one steal, in a 121–114 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Greenspan|title=Lowry leads depleted Raptors past Lakers; LeBron exits early|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/2021/05/03/lowry-leads-depleted-raptors-past-lakers-lebron-exits-early.html|work=TheStar.com|date=May 3, 2021|access-date=May 4, 2021}} On October 13, 2021, Gillespie was waived by the Raptors.{{cite web|title=Raptors Waive Gillespie and Perry|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-gillespie-and-perry|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 13, 2021|date=October 13, 2021}} ===Return to the Hustle (2021) === On October 23, 2021, Gillespie re-signed with the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Moore|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2021–22 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster-211023/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} In 12 games, he averaged 11.4 points, 12.2 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 2.75 blocks and 1.17 steals in 33.2 minutes per game, leading the team in rebounding and leading the entire league in blocked shots.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Tim Frazier and Freddie Gillespie to 10-Day Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-tim-frazier-and-freddie-gillespie-10-day-contracts-20211220|website=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} ===Orlando Magic (2021–2022)=== On December 21, 2021, Gillespie signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]]. He signed a second 10-day contract with the team on December 31.{{cite web |title=Orlando Magic Sign Tim Frazier and Freddie Gillespie to Second 10-Day Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-tim-frazier-freddie-gillespie-second-ten-day-contract-20211231 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=December 31, 2021}} ===Third stint with the Memphis Hustle (2022)=== On January 10, 2022, Gillespie was reacquired and activated by the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 10, 2022|access-date=January 10, 2022}} ===Bayern Munich (2022–2023)=== [[File:2022-11-10 ALBA Berlin gegen FC Bayern München (EuroLeague 2022-23) by Sandro Halank–098.jpg|thumb|right|Gillespie with Bayern München in 2022]] On July 25, 2022, Gillespie signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] until 2024.{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bayern-basketball-signs-freddie-gillespie-2024/|title=Bayern Basketball officially signs Freddie Gillespie|last=|first=|date=July 25, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 8, 2022|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} ===Crvena zvezda (2023–2024)=== On December 18, 2023, Gillespie left Bayern Munich and signed with Serbian club [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] for the rest of the season.{{cite web |title=Freddie Gillespie shifts from Bayern to Crvena Zvezda |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1598973/freddie-gillespie-signs-with-crvena-zvezda-euroleague/ |website=eurohoops.net |access-date=July 25, 2024 |date=December 18, 2023}} On June 10, 2024, he parted ways with the team.{{cite web |title=Crvena Zvezda parted ways with Mike Tobey and Freddie Gillespie |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1683207/crvena-zvezda-mike-tobey-freddie-gillespie-euroleague-aba-league/ |website=eurohoops.net |access-date=July 25, 2024 |date=June 10, 2024}} ===New Zealand Breakers (2024)=== On July 25, 2024, Gillespie signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2024–25 NBL season|2024–25 season]].{{cite web |title=Petteri Koponen Makes Huge Import Signing |url=https://www.nzbreakers.basketball/news/petteri-koponen-makes-huge-import-signing |website=nzbreakers.basketball |access-date=July 25, 2024 |date=July 25, 2024}} On September 15, he received a one-match suspension after an incident in which he headbutted [[Shaun Bruce]] of the [[Sydney Kings]].{{cite web |title=Breakers accept Gillespie suspension |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-accept-gillespie-suspension |website=NBL |access-date=September 29, 2024 |date=September 15, 2024}} He was granted a release from his contract on November 18, 2024.{{cite news |title=Gillespie granted release from BNZ Breakers |url=https://www.nzbreakers.basketball/news/gillespie-granted-release-from-bnz-breakers |access-date=18 November 2024 |work=nzbreakers.basketball |date=18 November 2024}} ===Olimpia Milano (2024)=== On November 19, 2024, Gillespie signed with Italian team [[Olimpia Milano]] for the remainder of the 2024-25 season.{{cite web |title=Freddie Gillespie Signs with Milan |url=https://basketnews.com/news-215085-freddie-gillespie-signs-with-milan.html |website=BasketNews |access-date=5 December 2024}} On March 6, 2025, with just more than two minutes of playing time in the second half, Gillespie suffered a scary blow to the head landing on the court after colliding with [[Devon Hall]] on a loose ball. He was unconsciousness for a few seconds and then left the court on a stretcher.{{cite web |title=Freddie Gillespie forced to leave the court against Fenerbahce after scary injury |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1794211/freddie-gillespie-milan-fenerbahce-euroleague-head-blow-injury-2024-2025/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=11 March 2025 |language=en |date=6 March 2025}} ===Galatasaray (2025–2026)=== On September 22, 2025, Gillespie signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.galatasaray.org/haber/basketbol/erkek-basketbol/galatasaray-mct-technic-e-hos-geldin-freddie-gillespie/58495|title=Galatasaray MCT Technic’e
